name: Adamax
status: Research chemical; Very limited direct human evidence
short: Adamax is best understood as a modified Semax-family nootropic rather than as an approved medication. The advertised purpose is longer-lasting cognitive and neuroprotective signaling after intranasal use, mainly by improving chemical stability and possibly ext

name: Adipotide
status: Animal/nonhuman-primate efficacy signal; Phase 1 initiated; No published human obesity-efficacy data; Renal safety concern
short: Adipotide is a targeted pro-apoptotic fat-vasculature compound. The animal data are notable, especially the obese-rhesus-monkey study, but the mechanism is tissue injury rather than reversible hormone signaling. Human development reached a Phase 1 setting in o

name: AHK-Cu
status: Cosmetic/topical hair and skin peptide; Systemic PK not established
short: AHK-Cu is a copper-binding tripeptide used mainly in topical scalp and skin products. It is discussed for hair-follicle signaling and dermal remodeling, not for whole-body hormone effects.

name: AOD-9604
status: Human safety data exist; Obesity efficacy remains limited/contested
short: AOD-9604 is a modified fragment of human growth hormone intended to isolate fat-metabolism signaling without full hGH activity.

name: ARA-290
status: Human clinical research for neuropathy/inflammation; Not broadly approved
short: ARA-290, also called cibinetide, is engineered from erythropoietin biology but is designed not to increase red blood cell production. Its intended target is the innate repair receptor, which is upregulated during tissue stress and injury.

name: BPC-157
status: Mostly preclinical/anecdotal; Major anti-doping and regulatory caution
short: BPC-157 is the most widely discussed “repair peptide” in the wellness and biohacking world. The repair story is plausible because the molecule has strong preclinical data in tendon, ligament, muscle, vascular, and gastrointestinal injury models. The limitation

name: Cagrilintide
status: Late-stage pharmaceutical obesity program
short: Cagrilintide is an amylin analog. In the CagriSema combination, it is paired with semaglutide so that one component strengthens satiety/satiation signaling while the GLP-1 component reduces appetite and improves glycemic control.

name: Cerebrolysin
status: Peptide mixture with regional medical use; Heterogeneous evidence
short: Cerebrolysin is not one peptide. It is a mixture of low-molecular-weight neuropeptides and amino acids derived from porcine brain tissue. That makes it different from a single-sequence synthetic peptide with one half-life and one receptor target.

name: CJC-1295
status: Human PK data for DAC form; Common confusion between DAC and no-DAC
short: CJC-1295 is a growth-hormone-releasing hormone analog. The single most important distinction is whether the product has DAC. No-DAC products behave like short GHRH pulses; DAC products bind albumin and last for days.

name: Dermorphin
status: Potent opioid peptide; Not a wellness peptide
short: Dermorphin is a mu-opioid receptor agonist peptide. It belongs in the guide because it is a peptide, but it should not be grouped mentally with repair, cosmetic, or metabolic peptides.

name: Dihexa
status: Experimental nootropic; Preclinical evidence with research-integrity cautions
short: Dihexa is a synthetic angiotensin-IV-derived compound marketed as a cognitive and neurorepair peptide. For a beginner, the key point is that it is not an approved medicine and not a clinically validated nootropic. It is better understood as a research compound

name: DSIP / Emideltide
status: Sleep-wake / withdrawal research peptide; Old human studies, unresolved mechanism
short: DSIP stands for delta sleep-inducing peptide. The FDA name used in the 2026 compounding review is Emideltide. It is a nine-amino-acid peptide that became famous because early rabbit experiments suggested it could increase slow-wave, delta-like EEG activity. In

name: Epithalon
status: Bioregulator/longevity peptide; Limited modern human evidence
short: Epithalon, also spelled Epitalon or Epithalone, is a synthetic tetrapeptide with the sequence Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly (AEDG). It is most often discussed in longevity communities because of its association with pineal bioregulation, circadian rhythm, melatonin signalin

name: FOXO4 and FOXO4-DRI
status: Preclinical senolytic concept; No human PK or steady-state model
short: FOXO4-DRI is a senolytic peptide concept designed to interfere with survival signaling in senescent cells. The goal is selective removal of damaged cells that resist apoptosis, not general stimulation.

name: GHK-Cu
status: Topical/local skin and scalp rationale is stronger than injectable/systemic evidence
short: GHK-Cu is a copper-binding tripeptide most defensibly discussed for topical/local skin and scalp signaling.

name: GHRP-6 & GHRP-2
status: Older GH secretagogues; Real endocrine effect with higher side-effect burden
short: GHRP-2 and GHRP-6 are ghrelin-receptor agonists that stimulate growth-hormone release. They can also affect hunger, prolactin, cortisol, glucose, and water retention.

name: Glutathione
status: Endogenous antioxidant system; Route and formulation matter
short: Glutathione is a tripeptide antioxidant made from glutamate, cysteine, and glycine. It supports redox balance, detoxification, and cellular defense.

name: Hexarelin
status: Potent GH secretagogue; Higher endocrine spillover and desensitization risk
short: Hexarelin, also called examorelin, is a synthetic GH secretagogue in the GHRP family. It is known for strong GH release and potential cardiovascular research interest.

name: HGH Fragment 176-191
status: Fat-metabolism fragment; Human efficacy uncertain
short: HGH Fragment 176-191 is a short C-terminal portion of the growth hormone molecule promoted for fat metabolism. It is not full growth hormone and should not be treated as the same product as AOD-9604.

name: hMG
status: Prescription fertility medicine; Not a casual peptide stack
short: hMG contains gonadotropin activity, mainly FSH with LH activity depending on preparation. It is used in reproductive medicine to stimulate ovarian follicles or support spermatogenesis in selected endocrine contexts.

name: Human Chorionic Gonadotropin
status: Approved fertility/endocrine drug with established medical uses
short: hCG is an LH-like hormone used medically in fertility and endocrine care. In men, it can stimulate Leydig cells to produce testosterone; In women, it can trigger ovulation in supervised protocols.

name: Humanin
status: Mitochondrial-derived cytoprotective peptide; Strong preclinical signal, limited human intervention data
short: Humanin is a small peptide made from a short open reading frame inside the mitochondrial 16S rRNA region. It is best understood as a cellular stress-response and survival signal, not as an approved anti-aging injection.

name: IGF-1 LR3
status: Potent growth-factor analog; High-risk gray-market use
short: IGF-1 LR3 is a modified insulin-like growth factor designed to last longer and bind IGF-binding proteins differently than native IGF-1. It is discussed for muscle growth and recovery, but the biology also overlaps with glucose lowering and cell-growth signalin

name: Ipamorelin
status: Selective GH secretagogue; Still not a benign wellness shortcut
short: Ipamorelin is a ghrelin-receptor agonist used to stimulate GH release with less cortisol and prolactin spillover than older GHRPs.

name: KPV
status: Anti-inflammatory tripeptide with early gut/skin interest
short: KPV is the C-terminal tripeptide of alpha-MSH and is discussed for anti-inflammatory effects, especially in gut and skin contexts.

name: Melanotan I
status: FDA-approved MC1R agonist for EPP; Not a cosmetic tanning protocol
short: Melanotan I is the older research name for afamelanotide, the active drug in SCENESSE. Unlike Melanotan II, it has an FDA-approved prescription form: a 16 mg controlled-release implant for adults with erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP).

name: Melanotan II
status: Nonselective melanocortin analog; High cosmetic-risk profile
short: Melanotan II is a melanocortin agonist best known for tanning and sexual arousal effects. Because it is nonselective, it can affect pigmentation, appetite, nausea pathways, sexual function, and cardiovascular/autonomic symptoms.

name: MOTS-c
alias: Mitochondrial Open Reading Frame of the 12S rRNA Type-C
status: Mitochondrial-derived peptide; Early translational evidence
short: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid mitochondrial-derived peptide. It is discussed as an “exercise mimetic” or metabolic-signaling peptide because it is linked to skeletal-muscle metabolism, AMPK-related pathways, insulin sensitivity, and stress adaptation.

name: NAD+
status: Endogenous coenzyme; Not a peptide
short: NAD+ is a coenzyme involved in energy metabolism, sirtuin activity, DNA repair, and cellular stress responses. It appears in peptide-clinic settings because it is often injected or infused, not because it is chemically a peptide.

name: Pinealon
status: Bioregulator peptide with limited clinical evidence
short: Pinealon is a short EDR tripeptide discussed for neuroprotection, cognitive aging, and bioregulator concepts.

name: Retatrutide
status: Late-stage investigational triple agonist
short: Retatrutide activates GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon receptors. The glucagon component is the key differentiator from tirzepatide and may contribute to greater energy-expenditure and liver-fat effects, but it may also change tolerability.

name: Selank
status: Neuroactive anxiolytic peptide; Human evidence mostly regional/limited
short: Selank is a synthetic analog related to tuftsin and is discussed for anxiety, stress resilience, and cognition. It is commonly used intranasally in community settings.

name: Semaglutide
status: Approved pharmaceutical GLP-1 therapy
short: Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist with approved uses in diabetes, obesity/weight management, and cardiovascular-risk contexts depending on product and label. It is not a research peptide in the same sense as BPC-157 or MOTS-c.

name: Semax
status: Russian-developed neuropeptide; Limited Western clinical confirmation
short: Semax is an ACTH 4-10 analog designed to keep neuroactive properties without broad endocrine ACTH effects. It is used intranasally in Russian medical practice for neurologic and cognitive indications.

name: Sermorelin
status: GHRH analog with established pharmacology; Off-label wellness use varies
short: Sermorelin is the first 29 amino acids of growth-hormone-releasing hormone. It stimulates the pituitary to release growth hormone, so it requires a responsive pituitary rather than bypassing the axis like direct hGH.

name: SS-31
status: Approved for Barth syndrome; Broader mitochondrial uses remain investigational
short: SS-31, now approved as elamipretide under the FORZINITY label, targets cardiolipin in the inner mitochondrial membrane. The approved use is narrow.

name: TB-500
alias: Identity-dependent: TB-500/LKKTETQ fragment vs full-length thymosin beta-4/Tβ4
status: Product-identity problem; Preclinical wound-healing rationale
short: TB-500 is commonly marketed as a tissue-repair peptide related to thymosin beta-4, but the name is not precise. In FDA compounding safety-risk language, TB-500 refers to the thymosin beta-4 fragment LKKTETQ. Full-length thymosin beta-4/Tβ4 is a different 43-am

name: Tesamorelin
status: FDA-approved GHRH analog for HIV-associated lipodystrophy
short: Tesamorelin is an approved GHRH analog used to reduce excess visceral abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. It is not simply a generic belly-fat peptide for everyone.

name: Thymosin Alpha-1
status: Immune-modulating peptide; Evidence is indication-specific
short: Thymosin alpha-1 is an immune-modulating peptide used in some countries as thymalfasin. It is discussed for antiviral, sepsis, vaccine-response, and immune-support contexts.

name: Tirzepatide
status: Approved pharmaceutical dual GIP/GLP-1 therapy
short: Tirzepatide is a dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist approved for type 2 diabetes and chronic weight management, with additional label expansion depending on current product status. It is a prescription drug, not a research peptide.

name: Vilon
status: Ultrashort thymic bioregulator; Mostly Russian/Eastern European preclinical and low-certainty clinical literature
short: Vilon is a two-amino-acid peptide: lysine plus glutamic acid, abbreviated Lys-Glu or KE. It is usually marketed as a thymus/immune-aging bioregulator. It is not the same as thymosin alpha-1, thymalin, thymogen, or hCG/hMG.

name: 5-Amino-1MQ
status: Investigational small molecule; Not a peptide
short: 5-Amino-1MQ is included because peptide clinics and metabolic-stacking discussions often mention it, but chemically it is not a peptide. It is usually discussed as an NNMT inhibitor related to fat-cell metabolism and NAD salvage pathways.

name: Bacteriostatic Water
status: Diluent/preservative product; Not a peptide and not pharmacologically active
short: Bacteriostatic water is sterile water containing benzyl alcohol preservative. It is used as a diluent for some multi-dose products, not as a peptide therapy.
